central_law.provision: MV Act 1988 s.129 read with s.194D (inserted by Act 32 of 2019, s.79)

offences.label: Using a handheld communication device while driving

central_law.provision: MV Act 1988 s.184, Explanation (c) (inserted by Act 32 of 2019, s.67); compounding under s.200(1) limited to this use (Act 32 of 2019, s.86)
central_law.penalty_text: First offence: imprisonment of six months to one year, or fine of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000, or both. Second or subsequent offence within three years: imprisonment up to two years, or fine of ten thousand rupees, or both.
central_law.note: Earphones or headphones for music are not named in s.184, the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations 2017, or 208-WT. See docs/FINDINGS.md, claim C2.

state_compounding.note: The row reads 'Driving dangerously, s.184'; the subsequent amount applies if committed within three years of a previous similar offence. Because s.200(1) allows s.184 to be compounded only for handheld-device use, this row is mapped to that offence here.

observations.summary: 184MVA/184MVA, 'Driving Vehicle Dangerously. No Person Shall Use Earphone While Driving Any Motor Vehicles': Rs 5000 first, Rs 10000 subsequent.
218(3) WBMVR/177MVA, playing radio or mobile phone in a motor vehicle in a city or municipality: Rs 500 first, Rs 1500 subsequent.

central_law.provision: MV Act 1988 s.184, Explanation (a) (inserted by Act 32 of 2019, s.67)
central_law.penalty_text: Listed as driving dangerously: first offence imprisonment of six months to one year, or fine of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000, or both.
central_law.note: s.200(1) as amended allows s.184 to be compounded only for handheld-device use, so a spot amount for red-light jumping needs a different legal basis.

state_compounding.settle_with: 208-WT has no row that names signal violations. A legal review must settle which penal section applies to red-light jumping after Act 32 of 2019 (s.184 Explanation (a) versus s.177 or s.177A with the Driving Regulations 2017), and then which 208-WT row, if any, sets the amount.
